name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-30 'Longframe'
description:
The KP-30 is Kang-Petrov's extended-frame competition and duty variant, built around a 153mm barrel with an integral compensator milled into the slide — not a ported barrel but a proper stepped compensator with two transverse slots that redirect propellant gas upward and reduce muzzle flip by roughly 35% over a standard KP-19 in back-to-back testing. The frame is full-size with a lengthened dust cover that accommodates a factory accessory rail capable of handling lights, laser aiming modules, or the Slagworks-branded SL-2 foregrip stub. Magazine capacity is 21 rounds of 9x19mm Standard in a double-stack extended basepad configuration. The trigger is a factory-tuned flat-face unit with a 2.4kg pull — lighter than the standard KP trigger — and the slide serrations are aggressive front-and-rear rather than the rear-only pattern on cheaper models.

The KP-30 sits at the upper edge of what Tier 1 money can access — it's priced at Φ620, which is real money for a shelf worker, and the people who buy it tend to be the kind of Tier 1 earner who takes their personal defense seriously enough to spend three weeks of discretionary income on a pistol. Mid-tier private security firms sometimes issue them to squad leaders as a prestige marker — a visible signal that the person carrying it has been deemed worth the investment. The competition shooting community in GLMZ, such as it is, runs the KP-30 because it's the best platform-legal gun available without crossing into Tier 2 restricted territory.

A KP-30 in good condition has a particular look — the compensator slots develop carbon scoring patterns that are almost decorative, and the flat-face trigger shows wear in a precise horizontal stripe from the trigger finger pad. Owners who actually shoot them tend to be proud in a quiet, competent way. Owners who bought them for status tend to have pristine examples with four rounds through them, kept in the box. You can always tell the difference by looking at the compensator.
specifications:
caliber: 9x19mm Standard

tactical_use: The KP-30's compensated slide makes it unusually controllable for rapid follow-up shots, and the extended barrel adds meaningful velocity at the ranges where 9mm starts to lose authority. Operators running the KP-30 with an accessory light can clear confined spaces with a weapon that handles like a service pistol while carrying a 21-round capacity. The longer frame makes concealed carry impractical, so users who run this gun are typically making a statement: they are armed, they know how to use it, and they have enough rounds not to be immediately concerned about counting them.
cultural_context: The KP-30 occupies an interesting status position in GLMZ — it's the nicest gun a Tier 1 person can buy without it being weird, and the cheapest gun a Tier 2 person would consider carrying. Security shift supervisors wear them openly on patrol in a way that communicates competence. In the Gray Zone worker competition shooting leagues that run out of the Calumet industrial parks on weekends, the KP-30 is the prestige entry — not the gun of champions, but the gun of someone who takes it seriously enough to matter.
known_users: Tier 1 business owners who can afford to upgrade
private protection contractors working Tier 2 clients on a Tier 1 budget
story_hooks: A KP-30 with an aftermarket trigger job and hand-lapped barrel shows up at a Calumet shooting league — the gunwork is professional military grade, way beyond what any local smith could do, and the owner claims he bought it at a swap meet.

A shelf cooperative's elected security chief was just found with her KP-30 drawn and unfired, dead of what the ACS report calls 'cardiac event' — but she was 31 years old and her last medical showed a clean bill of health.
